question.problem:
In a nutrition study, the mass of bacteria in a culture (in $\text{g}$) after $t$ hours is given by the function $M(t).$ The values of $M(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| **$t$** | $1.5$ | $1.8$ | $2.1$ | $2.4$ | $2.7$ | $3.0$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **$M(t)$** | $6.2$ | $6.8$ | $7.5$ | $8.1$ | $8.7$ | $9.3$ |

Approximate the bacteria’s mass instantaneous rate of change at $t=2.4$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=0.3.$

The bacteria’s mass at $t=2.4$ is changing at approximately 
{{field-1}} $g$ per hour.
question.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{M}^{′}(t)≈\frac{M(t+h)-M(t-h)}{2h},
$$

at time $t=2.4$ with step size $h=0.3.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}^{′}(2.4) & ≈\frac{M(2.4+0.3)-M(2.4-0.3)}{2(0.3)} \\  & =\frac{M(2.7)-M(2.1)}{0.6} \\  & =\frac{8.7-7.5}{0.6} \\  & =\frac{1.2}{0.6} \\  & =2.0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the bacteria’s mass at $t=2.4$ is changing at approximately $2.0\,g$ per hour.
